notes: `בָרִאשֹׁנָה` and `בָּאַחֲרֹנָה` each leave preposition and assimilated article `unrepresented` under rules 40 and 29: the adjective holds the whole written word, so rule 40's closing fusion case (where the governed word keeps no English of its own) does not reach them.
`יַד הָעֵדִים` and `יַד כָּל־הָעָם` are rule 29's arthrous case, not fronting: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one.
`מִקִּרְבֶּךָ` is split rather than fused — the ASV writes *from*, *the midst* and *of thee*, so each morpheme has a rendering of its own and rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet.
